description: Add a way to export a session's PRD and TRD as a downloadable PDF instead of just viewing markdown in the browser.

answers.question: Should the export be a button on the results page, or a separate route?
answers.answer: A button on the results page next to the existing tabs.

answers.question: Should generated PDFs be stored, or generated on demand each time?
answers.answer: Generated on demand, no storage needed.

answers.question: Anyone with the session link, or only the session creator?

description: Add rate limiting to the API so one client can't hammer the LLM-backed endpoints and run up the bill.

answers.question: Should rate-limited requests get a 429 with a retry-after, or silently queue?
answers.answer: 429 with retry-after, keep it simple.

answers.question: Per-IP limits or per-session limits?
answers.answer: Not sure, whatever's easiest to ship first.

answers.question: Should this cover the static file routes too, or just /api?
answers.answer: Just /api.

description: Cache repo reads so re-running the pipeline against the same repo path doesn't re-walk the whole filesystem every time.

answers.question: Should there be a way to force a fresh scan, bypassing the cache?
answers.answer: Yes, a flag or query param to force refresh.

answers.question: In-memory cache or persisted to Postgres?
answers.answer: In-memory is fine for now.

answers.question: Does this affect the git-clone path (temp dirs) too, or only local paths?

description: Add user authentication so sessions are scoped to a logged-in user instead of anyone with the session id being able to view it.

answers.question: Email/password login, or an OAuth provider?
answers.answer: Email/password is fine for v1.

answers.question: Does the sessions table need a user_id column, or a separate join table?
answers.answer: A user_id column on sessions should be enough.

answers.question: Should this also gate the GitHub write-back endpoint, or is that already implicitly protected by needing a PAT?
answers.answer: Gate it too, for consistency.

description: Let users edit and resubmit their answers after seeing the PRD/TRD, without having to start a whole new session.

answers.question: Should resubmitting re-run the whole pipeline, or just regenerate the docs?
answers.answer: Re-run the whole pipeline, answers might change findings too.

answers.question: Should old findings/documents be overwritten or versioned?
answers.answer: Whatever is simplest, versioning can come later.

answers.question: Should this be limited to sessions that haven't been pushed to GitHub yet?
answers.answer: Good question, yes let's limit it to that.

description: Add a way to automatically delete sessions older than 30 days to keep the database from growing unbounded.

answers.question: Should this run as a scheduled job, or on-demand via an admin endpoint?
answers.answer: A scheduled job, doesn't need to be triggered manually.

answers.question: Hard delete or soft delete (a deleted_at column)?
Should this also clean up cloned temp repo directories from the git-clone path?
answers.answer: Not sure, hadn't thought about that.

description: Add password reset via email for users who forgot their password.

answers.question: Should the reset link expire after a set time?
answers.answer: Yes, 1 hour expiry.

answers.question: Does the User model need a password hash field currently, and does it need a reset-token field added?
answers.answer: Need to add a reset token field, not sure what exists currently.

answers.question: All users, or only ones who signed up with email/password (vs SSO, if that ever exists)?
answers.answer: All users for now, there's no SSO.

description: Add pagination to the users list endpoint so it doesn't return the whole table at once.

answers.question: Page-number based or cursor based pagination?
answers.answer: Page-number based, simplest for the frontend.

answers.question: What should the default and max page size be?
answers.answer: 20 default, 100 max.

answers.question: Should sorting/filtering be added at the same time, or strictly pagination only?

description: Support file uploads so users can set a profile avatar image.

answers.question: Should there be client-side image cropping, or just accept whatever's uploaded?
answers.answer: Just accept it for v1, no cropping.

answers.question: Store the image on disk with a path column, or in a blob store?
answers.answer: Disk with a path column is fine to start.

answers.question: Any file size or type restrictions needed?
answers.answer: Yes, images only, some reasonable size cap.

description: Add a health check endpoint for the load balancer to hit.

answers.question: Should it just return 200 OK, or also check DB connectivity?
answers.answer: Check DB connectivity too, that's the whole point.

answers.question: No new data model needed here, correct?
answers.answer: Correct, none needed.

answers.question: Should this expose any other service metrics, or strictly up/down?
answers.answer: Strictly up/down.

description: Migrate the server-rendered templates to use a proper frontend framework instead of Jinja templates.

answers.question: Should this be a gradual page-by-page migration, or a full rewrite?
answers.answer: Gradual, page by page.

answers.question: Does the backend need to expose new JSON API endpoints for the pages being migrated?
answers.answer: Yes, probably.

answers.question: Which framework, if you have a preference?
answers.answer: No strong preference, whatever's simplest.

description: Add a dark mode toggle to the dashboard.

answers.question: Should the preference persist across sessions?
answers.answer: Yes, remember the choice.

answers.question: Store the preference in localStorage, or on a user profile in the backend?
answers.answer: localStorage is fine, no backend needed.

answers.question: Should it follow system preference by default, or default to light?

description: Add client-side form validation to the signup form.

answers.question: Show errors inline as the user types, or only on submit?
answers.answer: Inline as they type, better UX.

answers.question: Does this need a validation library, or hand-rolled checks?
answers.answer: Whatever's simplest, no strong opinion.

answers.question: Is there an existing signup form in the codebase, or does this need to be built first?
answers.answer: Not sure, would need to check.

description: Add a loading skeleton while the dashboard data fetches, instead of a blank screen.

answers.question: Skeleton matching the final layout, or a generic spinner?
answers.answer: A skeleton matching the layout, looks more polished.

answers.question: No new data model needed here, correct?
answers.answer: Correct.

answers.question: Should this also cover error states, or strictly the loading state?
answers.answer: Strictly loading for this pass.

description: Add an error boundary so one broken component doesn't crash the whole app.

answers.question: Show a generic fallback message, or something component-specific?
answers.answer: A generic fallback is fine to start.

answers.question: Should errors be logged anywhere, or just caught and displayed?
answers.answer: Just caught and displayed for now.

answers.question: One top-level boundary, or one per major section?

description: Add unit tests for the API client module.

answers.question: N/A for this one -- any preference on test runner?
answers.answer: Whatever's already set up, if anything.

answers.question: Should network calls be mocked, or hit a test server?
answers.answer: Mocked, no test server available.

answers.question: Should this cover component tests too, or strictly the API client?
answers.answer: Strictly the API client for now.

description: Add role-based permissions so admins can do things regular users can't.

answers.question: Just admin vs regular user, or a fuller role system?
answers.answer: Just admin vs regular for now.

answers.question: Add a role column to the User model, or a separate roles table?
answers.answer: A role column is simplest.

answers.question: Which existing endpoints need to become admin-only?
answers.answer: Not sure yet, need to figure that out.

description: Add internationalization so the dashboard can support multiple languages.

answers.question: Which languages first?
answers.answer: English and Spanish to start.

answers.question: Store the language preference client-side, or per-user in a backend that doesn't exist yet?
answers.answer: Client-side, there's no backend for this app.

answers.question: Should this cover date/number formatting too, or strictly UI strings?
